hook.text: Batteries store roughly 50 times less energy per kilogram than jet fuel. That's a brutal limit for flight.

buildup.text: Small electric planes with seating for 2 to 9 passengers are flying test routes under 100 miles.

discovery.text: For short hops—island routes, commuter flights—electric planes could cut costs and emissions dramatically.

twist.text: Long-haul electric flight is physically implausible with current battery chemistry. The weight kills range.

climax.text: Hybrid-electric and hydrogen fuel cell planes are being tested for medium-range routes by Airbus and others.

punchline.text: Electric planes will fly—but only short distances, for now.

quiz.question: Why can't current batteries power long-haul flights?
options: They store about 50 times less energy per kilogram than jet fuel
